notes: Production code and retry tests are identical to C2's, but it adds no unit tests for the new Placeholders() API or the extraction helper in caddyhttp.

Works correctly and handles dynamic names, escaped literals and look-alike names, but it hardcodes reverse_proxy-specific placeholder names inside the generic caddyhttp CEL matcher, which is a layering leak; the integration test only covers the method expression.

Production code is identical to the reference, with focused tests for Placeholders() (including the returned-copy check), a ph() variant of the status-code retry test, and request-only integration cases for upstream.host, the escaped literal and status_codes.

Logic matches the reference, and the tests are thorough: a placeholder-extraction unit test, a table test of matcherSetReferencesResponse covering every case the maintainers named, integration tests that check the echoed POST body, and a direct ph() response-retry test; the small LoadBalancing doc update is relevant.
Same patch as C2/C3, matching the reference fix, with good coverage of every review requirement for both stream and datagram sockets.
Same patch as C2, matching the reference fix exactly, with the same thorough white-box tests for unlink-on-last-close, double close, concurrent relisten and abstract sockets.

A plausible redesign: a shared unixSocket keeps the original fd and gives each holder a dup that is closed on release, with abstract checks and CAS double-close guards. But it rewrites the internal types (removes the `count` field, changes the `unixSockets` map type, switches deleteListener/deletePacketConn to pointer receivers), which breaks the package so the hidden tests do not compile (0/7, suite failed) and goes well beyond the needed fix.

Identical to the reference: it closes the leaked dup in reuseUnixSocket, drops the leaking File() call in Close, adds the CAS double-close guard, unlinks under the mutex, and skips abstract sockets. Its tests cover immediate unlink, refcounting, double close, close/listen races and abstract sockets; the one wart is that the abstract-socket test writes a sentinel file into the package directory.

Sound zip change with extra seek-past-end handling, but the squashfs single-file root now requires `o.Remote() == path.Join(prefix, root)`, which is fragile if fromNative encodes names; tests are good, though the squashfs ones depend on mksquashfs being installed.
Identical to C5: reference-equivalent source, with lighter tests that lack range/seek and skip-agreement checks.
Same source as the reference, with an escape test and docs, but the tests skip range/seek and the NewObject-agreement-when-skipped checks.

Follows the reference's naming approach via exposedName, with good tests and docs, but silently swallows Readlink failures and returns an empty target, and zip does not exclude directory entries from symlink detection.

Correct, including suffixed roots via rootLinkAlias, but the squashfs New root logic is convoluted, the zip Open now treats EOF during seek as success for every object, and an existing test comment is rewritten for no reason.

Clean implementation: newObjectNative prefers a literal regular `.rclonelink` member, both suffixed and bare roots work, zip offsets are clamped, and tests use a checked-in squashfs fixture plus a copy-escape test.

Functionally works and dedups clashing names, but is hacky: deferred link insertion with a repeated CheckParents, a `dt[""] = nil` workaround, dead translatedRemote code, mutation of obj.remote after creation, and an unrelated sanitize.Leaf addition.
Source matches the reference exactly, and the tests are thorough: skip/NewObject agreement, range/seek, a regular `.rclonelink` member, a squashfs image and an end-to-end escape check, plus docs.

Works and handles the case where a symlink's suffixed name clashes with a regular member, but the two-pass zipEntry approach is heavy, the go-diskfs test uses a process-wide chdir, and a root pointing at the listed `x.rclonelink` name resolves to nothing while the unsuffixed name resolves to the link, so root handling disagrees with the listing.
